reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Four findings against `main`:

1. *P1 — The helpers never reach the cards.* `src/card.js:2` still returns the trimmed body unchanged; neither `excerpt` nor `toPlain` has a production caller. Cards therefore still show the full, unflattened body.
   *Fix:* Wire plain-text conversion and excerpting into the card-building path with the intended preview limit; add a card-level test.

2. *P1 — Short text loses content and always gets an ellipsis.* `src/excerpt.js:6–8` truncates without checking length. `excerpt('hello world', 20)` returns `"hello…"`, and empty input returns `"…"`. This contradicts the README’s unchanged-short-text contract.
   *Fix:* Return text unchanged when its length is at or below the limit; test shorter, exact-limit, and empty inputs.

3. *P2 — A word ending exactly at the limit is unnecessarily dropped.* `src/words.js:2–3` excludes the character at `limit` when searching for a space. `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `"one…"` even though `"one two…"` fits the documented cutoff.
   *Fix:* Include the boundary at `limit` in the search. Update `test/words.test.js`, whose current expectation encodes this bug.

4. *P2 — Markdown flattening deletes literal content.* `src/plain.js:3` removes every underscore, asterisk, tilde, and backtick, regardless of context. For example, inline code `` `user_id` `` becomes `userid`, changing the displayed identifier.
   *Fix:* Strip formatting delimiters without deleting characters inside their content; add cases for inline code and literal underscores.

All four existing tests pass, but they don’t catch these behaviors. No files changed.
